title: Asian Stocks Rally as Tame US Inflation Data Eases Fed Rate Hike Fears
excerpt: South Korean shares jumped 4.4% and Japan's Nikkei gained 1.9% after US consumer prices rose just 0.1% in July, dampening expectations of a September Fed rate increase.
body:
• Asian markets rallied Thursday after US consumer prices rose just 0.1% in July, in line with forecasts, pushing the probability of a September Fed rate hike down to 40% from 54% a week ago.
  • South Korean shares surged 4.4%, Japan's Nikkei gained 1.9%, and the MSCI Asia-Pacific index rose nearly 1%, extending gains from a Wall Street session that lifted the S&P 500 to 7,752.
  • Core US inflation matched its slowest annual pace since March 2021 at 2.5%, strengthening the case for the Fed to hold rates steady despite elevated oil prices tied to the US-Iran standoff.
  • Brent crude eased to $88.35 a barrel after a six-day rally, while gold climbed above $4,400 an ounce and the yen held near 159 per dollar amid growing expectations of a Bank of Japan rate hike in September.

Asian equities surged on Thursday as benign US inflation data took the edge off expectations for further Federal Reserve rate increases, sending relief across global markets that had been on edge over persistent price pressures and geopolitical risk.

The MSCI Asia-Pacific index rose 0.97%, led by South Korean shares jumping 4.4% and Japan's Nikkei gaining 1.86%. The rally followed a positive session on Wall Street, where the S&P 500 advanced 0.31% to 7,752.35 and the Nasdaq Composite climbed 0.65% to 26,617.60, boosted by upbeat results from AI cloud company CoreWeave.

CPI Data Shifts Rate Calculus

The catalyst was Wednesday's US consumer price report, which showed prices rose just 0.1% in July — exactly in line with expectations. More significantly, core CPI, which strips out volatile food and energy costs, advanced 0.2% month-over-month and 2.5% year-over-year, matching the slowest annual pace since March 2021.

The data prompted markets to reassess the odds of a September rate hike. CME Group's FedWatch tool showed traders pricing in a 40% probability of an increase, down from 54% a week earlier.

"The CPI reading and a cooler-than-expected jobs report may keep hawkish Fed officials at bay in September. However, we remain guarded on the near-term outlook for inflation amid volatile oil prices tied to the ongoing Middle East conflict."

— Gary Schlossberg, Global Strategist, Wells Fargo Investment Institute

Chris Zaccarelli at Northlight Asset Management noted that the report's significance lay in what it did not show. "The big surprise with a report that had no surprises is that a situation where inflation isn't reaccelerating, coupled with the most recent weak jobs report, gives the Fed more time to wait," he said.

Oil Eases, Geopolitical Risks Persist

Brent crude edged lower to $88.35 a barrel, snapping a six-day rally, while US crude slipped to $82.58. But oil markets remain elevated compared with earlier this year as US-Iran tensions continue to weigh on supply expectations.

Washington and Tehran remain deadlocked over efforts to end the conflict in the Gulf. President Donald Trump claimed the US has "total control" over the Strait of Hormuz, a statement swiftly rejected by Iran. The waterway, through which roughly a fifth of global oil passes, has seen reduced shipping traffic amid the standoff.

Dorian Carrell, head of multi-asset income at Schroders, said the firm expects "a gradual but messy de-escalation" but warned that reduced Hormuz traffic would put a floor on oil prices and maintain an energy-driven inflationary driver in the near to medium term.

Currency and Bond Markets

In currency markets, the Japanese yen held steady at 159.31 per dollar, with growing speculation that the Bank of Japan could hike rates at its September meeting — earlier than the previously expected December timeline. Markets are pricing in nearly a 60% chance of a quarter-point increase.

Japan's wholesale prices rose 7.2% year-over-year in July, highlighting broadening price pressures that reinforce the case for tighter monetary policy. Reserve Bank of Australia Assistant Governor Christopher Kent said the bank's three cash rate increases this year were having their intended effects.

The dollar index was broadly flat at 99.93. The benchmark US 10-year Treasury yield edged up to 4.688%, with a 30-year bond auction expected to price at the highest financing rate in 25 years following a $42 billion 10-year note sale that drew yields not seen since 2007.

Gold Climbs, Looking Ahead

Spot gold rose to $4,419 an ounce, benefiting from the softer rate outlook. Silver gained 0.3% to $65.50.

Markets now turn their attention to the August CPI report due before the September Federal Open Market Committee meeting. With oil prices still elevated and the US-Iran situation unresolved, traders will scrutinize every data point for clues on whether the Fed can afford to stay on hold.

S&P 500 earnings have been a counterweight to the macro uncertainty, with BofA noting that with 90% of results in, earnings per share are up 30% year-over-year excluding investment gains at Alphabet and Amazon, matching the strongest beat rate since 2021. JPMorgan raised its S&P 500 price target to 8,000 from 7,800.
